sections.overview: Labeo rosae Steindachner, 1894 is a freshwater cyprinid of the genus Labeo, native chiefly to the Lowveld river systems of southern Africa.
sections.identification: It can reach about 40 centimetres fork length; adults have a red-orange iris and conspicuous red tubercles on the snout, but eye colour alone cannot separate it from L. altivelis.
sections.habitat: It occupies warm Lowveld reaches of the Limpopo, Incomati and Phongolo systems, using sandy main-channel stretches as well as dams.
sections.diet: Its food includes algae, detritus and small invertebrates.
sections.behavior: It is an active fish that migrates upstream in summer and may leap over obstacles while moving through swollen rivers.
sections.reproduction: Its upstream summer migration is associated with breeding; published accounts report maturity from about 15 centimetres total length.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Labeo with L. altivelis and L. ruddi; recent genomic work cautions that traditional morphology-based Labeo groups do not always reflect evolutionary lineages.
sections.conservation: It was assessed as Least Concern in South Africa in 2017; assessors described it as widespread and common, with threats localized at that time.
